newsitem.title: UK: Alcoa aluminium probe call meets little response.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa aluminium probe call meets little response.

text.p: There was little immediate response from the London Metal Exchange (LME) and the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) to a call by Alcoa for a probe into the aluminium market.
Alcoa chief-executive Paul O'Neill is to ask the LME and the IPAI to look for ways to avoid manipulation in the market.

This was prompted by a rise in aluminium stocks last Friday when 10,000 tonnes was put on warrant in Rotterdam, which O'Neill said was rumoured to be have been done by LME ring-dealer Barclays Metals.
"We have no comment to make. We do not comment on press speculation," a senior Barclays Metals spokesman said.
The IPAI, which publishes data monthly on producer inventories, was not in a position to make an immediate response, and the LME was also not immediately available for comment, either.
